The leader also sends heartbeats with a nonzero ReadIndex context only to voting members. Therefore an observer cannot normally receive a voter-issued nonzero ReadIndex context through a legal transition and then confirm it as quorum support.
knowledge.conditions: The user-facing configuration-change and raft snapshot paths are used as captured; no direct mutation of internal role maps, operator role misconfiguration, forged messages, or a custom transport that changes response admission is included.

knowledge.statement: handleLeaderPropose inspects every proposed entry, reports a configuration-change entry as dropped and replaces it with an empty application entry when pendingConfigChange is already set, and sets that flag for each configuration-change entry it inspects before appending the remaining entries and replicating them. The apply paths addNode, addObserver, addWitness and removeNode clear the flag, and reset clears it on a term or role transition, so a leader that proposed a configuration change keeps refusing new configuration changes until a configuration change is applied or the peer changes term or role.
knowledge.conditions: The peer is leader, configuration-change proposals arrive through handleLeaderPropose, and configuration changes are applied through the raft apply paths and reported by the surrounding node.

knowledge.statement: handleNodeElection refuses to campaign when log.committed exceeds the applied index, using the general committed-versus-applied check rather than a configuration-specific one, so a node with any committed but unapplied entry cannot start an election. preLeaderPromotionHandleConfigChange then counts only configuration-change entries after the committed index and re-sets the pending flag when exactly one exists, or panics when more than one exists. handleFollowerTimeoutNow reaches the same election handler because it only advances the election tick and lets the normal tick emit the Election message, and tryCommit evaluates the cluster quorum from the raft membership maps that the apply paths maintain.
knowledge.conditions: Elections start through the Election message, including the path taken after a leader-transfer TimeoutNow, and the applied index is the value the surrounding node reports after its state machine applies entries.

knowledge.statement: engine.processSteps collects one update per active node, then sends only the messages node.sendReplicateMessages admits, which isFreeOrderMessage restricts to Replicate and Ping, before calling logdb.SaveRaftState for the whole update batch. SaveRaftState writes each non-empty raft state, the entries and snapshot metadata into one write batch that the log DB commits atomically, and only after that does processSteps call node.processRaftUpdate, which appends entries to the log reader and forwards every remaining message, including RequestVoteResp, HeartbeatResp and ReadIndexResp.
knowledge.conditions: The updates are produced by the execution engine's processSteps batch loop, each peer includes its changed raft state in the update, and the log DB implements SaveRaftState as one atomically committed write batch.

knowledge.statement: NodeHost.SyncRead resolves the caller context through linearizableRead, which calls the internal readIndex helper and node.read; node.read registers the request through pendingReadIndex.read and the helper then marks the node ready, so a synchronous read waits on the same pending batch the ReadIndex protocol completes. NodeHost.ReadIndex returns the RequestState from the same helper, and ReadLocalNode refuses to read unless that state's ready-to-read flag was set. The shared result mapping returns normally on a completed result, returns ErrTimeout on a timeout result or an expired caller context, ErrClusterNotReady on a dropped result, and ErrRejected, ErrClusterClosed or ErrAborted on the other result codes.
knowledge.conditions: The caller invokes these public APIs on an initialized non-witness node, and the read batch was registered through pendingReadIndex.read before the reply is processed.

knowledge.statement: On each heartbeat timeout leaderTick emits a LeaderHeartbeat, and handleLeaderHeartbeat broadcasts a heartbeat whose context is readIndex.peepCtx when a read is pending; peepCtx returns the last queued context, which is the newest admitted request. A follower echoes that Hint and HintHigh in its HeartbeatResp, and handleLeaderHeartbeatResp passes any nonzero hint to handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation, so a periodic heartbeat confirms the newest queued context and readIndex.confirm then returns every earlier queued request together with it.
knowledge.conditions: The node is leader with at least one pending ReadIndex request, and at least one voter responds to the periodic heartbeat carrying the newest context.

knowledge.statement: raft.restore rejects a snapshot whose index does not exceed the committed index, panics when the local node would become an observer or witness, and otherwise lets the log replace its state and set the committed and processed positions to the snapshot index. restoreRemotes then recreates the remotes, observers and witnesses maps from the snapshot membership, promoting a local observer to follower when the snapshot lists it as a full member, panicking on a witness promotion, and stepping a leader down when the snapshot no longer contains it. knowledge.statement: When a ReadIndex request is pending, broadcastHeartbeatMessage uses readIndex.peepCtx as the heartbeat context and broadcastHeartbeatMessageWithHint sends that hint-carrying heartbeat to every member of votingMembers(), which is the union of remotes and witnesses; observers are sent a heartbeat only when the context is zero. numVotingMembers() is len(remotes)+len(witnesses), and both quorum() and the commit path use it, so a witness acknowledgement counts toward the read quorum and the commit quorum alike. On the leader, a HeartbeatResp is admitted through lw, which resolves the sender against the current remotes, observers and witnesses maps and drops the message when it is in none of them; handleLeaderHeartbeatResp then passes a nonzero hint to handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation, and readIndex.confirm performs no further role check.
knowledge.conditions: The node is leader with at least one pending ReadIndex request, the role maps reflect the current configuration, and a heartbeat response arrives from a node that is currently a voter, an observer, a witness, or in no role map.

history.statement: When a ReadIndex request is pending, broadcastHeartbeatMessage uses readIndex.peepCtx as the heartbeat context and broadcastHeartbeatMessageWithHint sends that hint-carrying heartbeat only to current voting members; observers receive a heartbeat only when the context is zero, and witnesses are not addressed. On the leader, a HeartbeatResp is admitted through lw, which resolves the sender against the current remotes, observers and witnesses maps and drops the message when it is in none of them, after which handleLeaderHeartbeatResp passes a nonzero hint to handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation and readIndex.confirm counts the admitted sender without a further role check.
history.conditions: The node is leader with at least one pending ReadIndex request, the role maps reflect the current configuration, and a heartbeat response arrives from a node that is currently a voter, an observer, a witness, or in no role map.

knowledge.statement: NodeHost.SyncRead calls nh.linearizableRead with a Lookup callback. linearizableRead takes the timeout from the caller context, calls nh.readIndex, and that helper calls node.read with nh.getTimeoutTick(timeout) before marking the engine step ready. node.read rejects an uninitialized node with ErrClusterNotReady and a witness with ErrInvalidOperation, and otherwise registers the request through pendingReadIndexes.read. linearizableRead then waits on getRequestState(ctx, rs), releases the request state and runs the callback. NodeHost.ReadIndex resolves the same nh.readIndex helper and returns its RequestState to the caller.
knowledge.conditions: The caller invokes SyncRead or ReadIndex on an initialized cluster with a context that carries a deadline, and production code is unchanged.

knowledge.statement: NodeHostConfig.GetTargetValidator returns id.IsNodeHostID when AddressByNodeHostID is set, the transport factory's Validate when a TransportFactory is configured, and stringutil.IsValidAddress otherwise. node.requestConfigChange calls that predicate for every change whose type is not RemoveNode and returns ErrInvalidAddress when it fails, before constructing the ConfigChange that the membership state machine later validates.
knowledge.conditions: RequestAddNode or another non-remove membership request is issued on an initialized non-witness node, and the target is judged by the configured validator rather than by existing membership.

knowledge.statement: raft.reset replaces r.readIndex with a fresh readIndex, clears the vote and votes map, clears the pending configuration-change flag, aborts any leader transfer and rebuilds the remote, observer and witness maps. becomeCandidate, becomeLeader and the follower transition all call reset, so a pending ReadIndex request is dropped by any role transition, and a HeartbeatResp carrying its context in a later term cannot confirm it.
knowledge.conditions: The node performs a raft role transition through becomeFollower, becomeCandidate or becomeLeader while a ReadIndex request is pending.

knowledge.statement: The captured operational documentation describes adding an observer and later promoting it to a regular node while removing a failed node, and it states no requirement on the RequestAddNode target. knowledge.conditions: The captured tree is the source of documentation; no external documentation, changelog or issue tracker is consulted.

knowledge.statement: raft.restore rejects a snapshot whose index does not exceed the committed index, panics if the local node would become an observer or witness, and then, when the local log already matches the snapshot index and term, calls commitTo on that index and returns false without invoking log.restore or restoreRemotes. Otherwise it restores the log and returns true, and restoreRemotes later rebuilds the remote, observer and witness maps from the snapshot membership.
knowledge.conditions: A node receives or recovers from a snapshot whose index exceeds its committed index, and the local log either already matches the snapshot index and term or does not.

knowledge.statement: engine.processSteps takes one update per active node, calls applySnapshotAndUpdate, then for each update sends the free-order messages (Replicate and Ping) and calls processReadyToRead, processDroppedEntries and processDroppedReadIndexes, and only after that calls logdb.SaveRaftState for the whole batch. The remaining messages, including vote responses and read-index replies, are released by node.processRaftUpdate after the save. processReadyToRead passes its signals to pendingReadIndex.addReady and then applies LastApplied, and a batch completes only when the applied index reaches its ready index, so the pre-save release records a ready index without completing a read.
knowledge.conditions: The updates come from the engine's batch loop, each node includes its changed raft state, and the log DB implements SaveRaftState as one atomically committed write batch.

knowledge.statement: handleLeaderReadIndex rejects a follower-forwarded ReadIndex when the leader has no committed entry in its current term and calls reportDroppedReadIndex, which appends the forwarded message's SystemCtx to the leader's droppedReadIndexes list without sending anything to the requester. node.processDroppedReadIndexes passes each of those contexts to pendingReadIndex.dropped, which completes only requests in a batch keyed by that same context, so the leader has nothing to complete and the originating node's batch is untouched.

scope.description: Three in-process Raft peers with real Peer handlers and a test-only in-memory ILogDB. Nodes 2 and 3 issue ReadIndex requests with distinct SystemCtx values; the later context is confirmed first and the resulting reply for node 2 is routed through node 2's real follower handler and pendingReadIndex consumer.
assumptions: The three peers bootstrap membership {1,2,3}; node 1 is ticked until its current-term no-op commits.
The in-memory ILogDB preserves the ILogDB methods and indices needed for bootstrap, replication, and term lookup; it does not model disk failure, restart, or snapshots.

Both ReadIndex requests are queued at leader 1 before either heartbeat response is delivered. The later heartbeat is delivered to node 3 first, while the earlier heartbeat to node 2 is withheld. This is a controlled but ordinary reordering of same-term heartbeat responses.
The applied index for the pending batch is taken from the ReadyToRead produced by node 2's real follower handler, not invented.

No production code is modified. The client timeout is not waited for; completion is checked synchronously after applying the returned ready index, and the source pending-read timeout path remains the eventual endpoint.
excluded: No claim about every transport schedule, malicious peers, disk faults, snapshot restoration, witnesses, or observer-initiated reads.
No claim that every ReadIndex request times out; this probe concerns the demonstrated earlier-request/later-confirmation ordering.

scope.description: Logical-deadline case in the same three-peer in-process harness. A later context is confirmed first, node 2 receives the wrong context, its applied ReadyToRead leaves the original batch at index zero, and the pending-read clock is advanced past the caller's deadline.
assumptions: Real in-process Raft Peer handlers, a test-only in-memory ILogDB, and bootstrap membership {1,2,3}.
Node 2's read is created with a 50-tick timeout. The test applies the returned ReadyToRead index before advancing the logical clock.

excluded: This case measures the logical deadline and GC path, not real wall-clock scheduling or transport delay.

scope.description: Observer-local ReadIndex endpoint. The control case keeps the same setup and only delivers the observer's own confirmation first.

basis.prefix: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed, then records node 4 as an observer in each voter's raft membership through ApplyConfigChange. It calls Tick once on the leader and pumps it; the produced heartbeat addressed to node 3 carries the newest queued context. That heartbeat is delivered to node 3, its echo is returned to the leader, and the leader's replies are collected and grouped by address. The replies for node 2 and the reply for node 3 are emitted with their response contexts and indexes, then delivered to their nodes; the resulting ReadyToRead output and the confirmed index are fed to each node's pendingReadIndex, and the run records for each admitted read whether its batch still exists, its index and whether it completed.
basis.requirement: When one confirmation returns several earlier remote requests, each requester must receive a result tagged with its own SystemCtx and every admitted read must complete once the confirmed index is applied.
basis.responsibility: readIndex.confirm returns the queued requests up to the confirmed context, and handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation builds each remote reply from the confirming heartbeat's context; the requesting nodes' pendingReadIndex consume those replies. The experiment exercises those real handlers and changes only how many reads are queued and which node issues them.

interpretations.rationale: The current conclusion is a bounded liveness and client-contract defect for follower-originated ReadIndex requests, not a demonstrated stale-read safety failure. The retained execution admitted node 2's context {101,1002} as event 0 and node 3's context {202,2003} as event 1. Event 2 is a ReadIndex reply addressed to node 2 after node 3's confirmation; its response_ctx_low is node 3's context value, its response_log_index is 4, and leader_pending_after is zero. Event 3 shows node 2's original batch still exists but has index zero, while the real ReadyToRead index 4 was applied and completed_after_response is zero. Event 4 processes node 2's later context-101 confirmation and produces zero context-correct replies; completion remains zero. The source explains this without an unresolved intermediate link: readIndex.confirm returns all earlier queued requests with their original contexts, handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation substitutes the confirming heartbeat's Hint/HintHigh for the remote reply, and pendingReadIndex.addReady only updates the exact SystemCtx key. pendingReadIndex.applied completes only batches with a nonzero index not exceeding the applied index. The earlier queue entry was deleted by the later confirmation, so the later context-101 heartbeat cannot repair it. The request remains uncompleted after a valid applied index; the observed endpoint for this pending batch is the caller-supplied timeout path, although the harness did not wait for that interval. The reply's log index is 4, a later committed index, so the observation does not establish that a stale read value was returned. The existing read-index unit test expects earlier requests to retain their own contexts, which is consistent with the consumer requirement but does not exercise this remote batched ordering.

interpretations.rationale: The suspicion is refuted for the captured legal paths, although the low-level code alone would count it. handleLeaderHeartbeatResp confirms when a heartbeat response carries a nonzero hint, lw admits observer responses, and readIndex.confirm counts the responding node without checking whether it is currently a voter. That is the plausible weakness. The legal transition path does not create the needed state: membership rejects AddObserver or AddWitness for a current address; RemoveNode deletes the node from remotes, observers, and witnesses and marks it removed; isAddRemovedNode rejects re-adding that ID as any role; and raft.restore panics if a non-observer or non-witness local node appears in the snapshot's observer or witness set. In addition, broadcastHeartbeatMessageWithHint sends nonzero-context heartbeats only to votingMembers and sends observer heartbeats only for the zero context. A delayed response from a removed voter is therefore ignored because lw no longer finds it in any role map, and a delayed nonzero context cannot come from an observer under legal transitions. The rejoining-as-observer path is blocked by membership. The conclusion is a protective-mechanism negative result, not a claim that arbitrary direct map mutation or a malicious observer is safe; those are outside the admitted scenario and would still expose the low-level counting behavior.

interpretations.rationale: The suspicion is refuted for the captured raft paths. The hazard requires a leader whose log holds a committed configuration change that its membership maps have not yet applied, because tryCommit computes the quorum from those maps and a second change committed before the first is applied would be committed with the pre-change quorum. Two gates prevent that history. A leader that proposed a configuration change sets pendingConfigChange in handleLeaderPropose and keeps it set until a configuration-change apply path clears it, so any further configuration change it proposes is reported dropped and replaced with an empty application entry; the leader cannot accumulate a second uncommitted change while the first is committed but unapplied. A node that did not propose the change can only become leader by campaigning, and handleNodeElection refuses to campaign while log.committed exceeds the applied index, so a node that still has any committed unapplied entry, including a configuration change, cannot become leader; TimeoutNow cannot bypass this because it only advances the election tick and lets the normal tick emit the Election message that handleNodeElection gates. preLeaderPromotionHandleConfigChange therefore runs only after the applied index has caught up with the committed index, and its count of entries after the committed index is consistent with that state; it re-sets the pending flag for the single uncommitted change it can legitimately find and panics if the log ever holds more than one. The consequence is an availability tradeoff rather than the suspected safety violation: while the applied index lags, the node declines to campaign, and a leader keeps dropping configuration changes until the in-flight change is applied. The low-level pieces that suggested the hazard remain exactly as described, but the permitted leadership and proposal histories do not produce the required state.

interpretations.rationale: The suspicion that a granted vote could be lost before the vote response is sent is refuted for the captured batch path. processSteps takes one update per active node, emits only the messages that isFreeOrderMessage classifies as free order, which is Replicate and Ping, and then calls SaveRaftState for the whole batch; the log DB contract says that call atomically saves the raft states, log entries and snapshot metadata, and the implementation puts each non-empty state and the entries into one write batch that it commits once. The remaining messages travel in the same update through processRaftUpdate, which runs only after that commit, so RequestVoteResp, HeartbeatResp, ReplicateResp and ReadIndexResp are all emitted after the state that justifies them is durable. A crash after a vote response therefore cannot leave the previous vote or term in place, and the node cannot grant a different vote in the same term. The pre-persistence Replicate and Ping emission is the deliberate exception documented at the call site with a reference to section 10.2.1 of the Raft thesis; those messages carry no granted authority of their own, so the ordering that matters for election safety is preserved. counterevidence: The drop path only defers the read; the requester's own deadline still ends the wait, so no unbounded hang is established.
The leader-side drop is visible in its own update and through the warning log, so an operator can observe that reads were dropped even though the requester cannot.

A locally admitted read on a leader in the same state does receive ErrClusterNotReady through pendingReadIndex.dropped, which shows the notification mechanism exists and is simply not addressed to the remote requester.
limitations: This is a source-only account; no execution drives a follower-forwarded read into the not-ready branch and samples the caller endpoint.
It does not measure how long the not-ready window lasts after an election, which depends on how quickly the new leader commits its no-op.
